text:
pagerduty-bot: PAGING: High error rate on /v1/generate (prod-east) — 5xx spike, 12% error rate over 2 min. Severity: P1. Incident page: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-032
kyra (oncall): acked. I'm looking. any quick summary from monitoring?
alex (runtime): seeing a sudden model-mismatch error in prod-east: requests routed to rwd-ggml-v2 (quantized) but responses are failing validation (schema mismatch) — logs show tokenization errors and OOMs on a subset of instances.
sejin (ml-infra): that's odd — traffic policy for prod-east should prefer rwd-base-fp16, fallback to rwd-base-q4 when under load. How did rwd-ggml-v2 get routing?
lia (sre): also seeing region fallback churn: prod-east -> prod-central -> prod-east in a ~30s loop for a handful of routes, causing duplicate retries. Could be smart-routing policy mis-evaluating model compatibility.
kyra (oncall): timeline? when did it start?
alex (runtime): started 4m ago right after a spike in seq length for a big customer. The kernel-selection metric shows a mismatch, so the router picked the fastest compatible variant — rwd-ggml-v2 — but that variant wasn't registered for structured-output validation. Requests hit validation error path and retried -> routed to a different region -> back.
product-ops: FYI customer-impact: at least 3 accounts reported corrupted responses; 2 support tickets opened.
kyra (oncall): immediate mitigations? can we pin traffic to rwd-base-fp16 in prod-east while we debug?
sejin (ml-infra): we can force-model on the region, but note manual override bypasses autoscaler and routing safeties. If we force-model without capacity check, we risk queuing and more fallbacks.
kyra (oncall): I think risk is acceptable vs customers getting corrupt responses. I'll try force to base-fp16 with low concurrency.
kyra (oncall): Running override:
```
# force region model override
redwoodctl override set --region prod-east --model rwd-base-fp16 --mode force --concurrency 20 --expires 15m
```
deploy-bot: override accepted (id: ov-2026-1768881012). Change propagated to control-plane in ~8s.
lia (sre): seeing traffic shift — good. validation errors drop to 0. latency stable at 180ms.
alex (runtime): now seeing backlog on two fp16 instances; token generation rate limited due to concurrency cap. Some retries still hitting other regions which are now saturated and returning 429s.
kyra (oncall): product-ops — please update customers that we're forcing model to stable variant; monitoring for errors and latency.
product-ops: message queued to impacted customers.
sejin (ml-infra): caution — the override caused autoscaler to not spin up additional fp16 nodes in prod-east because override bypasses policy-based scaling. We should either: 1) increase concurrency limit, 2) lift override and fix policy, or 3) trigger capacity manually. What do you prefer?
kyra (oncall): option 3. Can you spin up 2 fp16 instances in prod-east?
sejin (ml-infra): spawning now. Using command:
```
redwoodctl capacity add --region prod-east --pool fp16 --count 2 --reason "incident: forced-model backlog"
```
deploy-bot: capacity request queued; expected ready in ~90s.
lia (sre): NOTE: while capacity is coming up, I'm seeing a secondary effect: several requests from a heavily multiplexed customer are being retried across regions due to prior 5xxs; those retries spike tokens and pushed router into a fallback-evaluation loop again. We might see another routing churn once capacity hits.
alex (runtime): I'm going to add a temporary retry-suppression header in the gateway for the impacted route to prevent cross-region retries: `X-RW-Retry-Mode: single` while we stabilize.
kyra (oncall): do it.
alex (runtime): patch applied to edge for route /v1/generate: `X-RW-Retry-Mode: single` — propagation done.
lia (sre): good, retries drop. capacity instances report healthy. throughput normalizing.
sejin (ml-infra): capacity online. removing the artificial concurrency cap? still have override in place for 10m. we can raise concurrency to 60 to absorb the backlog.
kyra (oncall): raise to 60.
sejin (ml-infra): updated override:
```
redwoodctl override update --id ov-2026-1768881012 --concurrency 60
```
deploy-bot: override updated.
kyra (oncall): looks stable now. errors back to baseline, latencies ~200ms. I want a root cause before removing override — alex, can you trace why rwd-ggml-v2 was considered compatible?
alex (runtime): early hypothesis: model capability metadata was out-of-sync in the control plane for a subset of routing decision caches — `supports_structured_output=false` mismatch. Router uses cached capability + sequence-length heuristics; for the spike paths it chose ggml-v2 as fastest. I'll gather traces.
product-ops: customers notified about temporary mitigation and ongoing investigation.
lia (sre): postmortem action: ensure override doesn't bypass autoscaler in the future, or make override option to optionally spin up capacity. noted.
kyra (oncall): agreed. Also add a guard that prevents routing to a model variant if schema-validation is unsupported.
sejin (ml-infra): one more thing — when we remove the override, we should roll it back carefully: removing override will allow router to rebalance and could send traffic to q4 variants which might be incompatible. Plan: 1) push capability fixes, 2) validate routing caches cleared, 3) remove override during low traffic window.
kyra (oncall): setting followup: postmortem + action items. I'll keep the override til 15:45 UTC and then coordinate rollback with runtime/infra. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
product-ops: noted, will file postmortem and the customer timeline.
pagerduty-bot: Incident updated to "mitigated" by kyra (oncall).
kyra (oncall): closing thread for now — will reopen if we see churn after rollback.
